entries.title: Job 7:1
segments: [Is there] not a warfare to man on earth? [Are] not his days also like the days of a hireling?

entries.title: Job 7:2
segments: As a servant earnestly desires the shadow, and as a hireling looks for his wages,

entries.title: Job 7:3
segments: so I am made to possess months of vanity, and weary nights are appointed to me.

entries.title: Job 7:4
segments: When I lie down, I say, When shall I rise? But the night is long, and I am full of tossing to and fro until the dawning of the day.

entries.title: Job 7:5
segments: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken and has run [afresh].

entries.title: Job 7:6
segments: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are ended without hope.

entries.title: Job 7:7
segments: Remember that my life [is] a breath; my eye shall no more see good.

entries.title: Job 7:8
segments: The eye of him who has seen me shall see me no [more]; Your eyes [are] on me, and I [am] gone.

entries.title: Job 7:9
segments: [As] the cloud falls and vanishes away, so he who goes down to the grave shall come up no [more].

entries.title: Job 7:10
segments: He shall return no more to his house, nor shall his place know him any more.

entries.title: Job 7:11
segments: Therefore I will not hold my mouth; I will speak in the trouble of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

entries.title: Job 7:12
segments: Am I like the sea, or a whale, that You set a watch over me?

entries.title: Job 7:13
segments: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint,

entries.title: Job 7:14
segments: then You scare me with dreams, and terrify me with visions;

entries.title: Job 7:15
segments: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my life.

entries.title: Job 7:16
segments: I despise [them]; I will not live always; let me alone, for my days [are] vanity.

entries.title: Job 7:17
segments: What [is] man, that You should magnify him, and that You should set Your heart on him,

entries.title: Job 7:18
segments: and visit him every morning, trying him every moment?

entries.title: Job 7:19
segments: Until when will You look away from me, nor let me alone until I swallow down my spittle?

entries.title: Job 7:20
segments: I have sinned. What shall I do to You, O Watcher of men? Why have You set me as a target for You, so that I am a burden to myself?

entries.title: Job 7:21
segments: And why do You not pardon my transgression, and take away my iniquity? For now I shall sleep in the dust, and You shall seek me in the morning, but I [shall] not be.
